rendered: The authors did not use a carbonate electrolyte because they judged it would form an unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the sodium metal anode. Instead, as opposed to traditional organic carbonate electrolytes, they assembled coin cells with NaPF6 salt dissolved in tetraglyme[1] as the electrolyte. The choice rested on earlier work emphasizing sodium anode stability during reversible plating in glymes. The electrolyte was chosen to overcome the unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes observed in[2] carbonate-based electrolytes[3], which the authors describe as critical to achieving good cycling performance. Their later discussion attributes the high Coulombic efficiency to stable SEI formation at the sodium metal-electrolyte interface, which they credit to the glyme electrolyte.
